findings.body:
**Route rejected FIXED verifications to the terminal-failure path.**

A `FIXED` result can fail `verify` or `module.mechanical` with a `ValueError`. That call sits outside the terminal-failure `except` clause at lines 376-394, so the exception leaves `harvest` before any terminal state is written. The run stays `queued`, and the next tick repeats the same failure.

Duplicate claimed commits trigger this deterministically. The check at lines 358-361 accepts repeated 40-hex SHAs, and `verify` rejects them with `ValueError` at `crq_repair/__init__.py:63-64`. A diff that `hack_detector` rejects follows the same path.

The caller isolates each item at `crq.py:3297-3300`, so other items still run. Only the affected item retries on every tick.

Handle `ValueError` in the FIXED block with the same terminal-failure sequence. Let other exceptions, such as git failures from `make_worktree`, propagate and retry.

<details>
<summary>Proposed change</summary>

```diff
                 check_wt, branch = c.make_worktree('verify-' + job_id, commits[-1])
                 try:
                     verify(check_wt, predecessor, commits, job_id)
                     from importlib import util
                     spec = util.spec_from_file_location('crq_repair_service', c.ROOT / 'crq_repair.py')
                     module = util.module_from_spec(spec)
                     spec.loader.exec_module(module)
                     module.mechanical(c.CONFIG, check_wt, predecessor, commits, job_id, path.parent)
+                except ValueError as exc:
+                    failure = {'job': job_id, 'item': item['id'], 'verdict': 'FAILED',
+                               'reason': 'invalid repair result: ' + str(exc)[:300],
+                               'finding': expected['finding']}
+                    if not dry:
+                        record['verdicts'] = verdicts + [failure]
+                        record.update(state='failed', error=str(exc)[:300])
+                        if item['kind'] == review_receipt.KIND:
+                            item['state'] = 'done'
+                            item['repair_outcome'] = record['state']
+                            item['last_error'] = None
+                        else:
+                            item['state'] = 'repair_failed'
+                            item['last_error'] = 'repair_failed; needs human'
+                        c.save_queue(q)  # terminal identity before authoritative write-back
+                        mark_finding_outcome(c, expected, failure)
+                    break
                 finally:
                     c.remove_worktree(check_wt, branch)
                 predecessor = commits[-1]
```

</details>
findings.title: Route rejected FIXED verifications to the terminal-failure path.

findings.body:
**Make the reviews fake drop later pages when `--paginate` is absent.**

`EndpointGh` returns the full review-page stream for every reviews request. Without `--paginate`, a real `gh api` call returns only the first page. The `reviews-paginated` case can therefore pass even if delivery stops paginating, and no named test asserts the flag directly.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
         if target.endswith("/reviews?per_page=100"):
             raw = self.reviews["stdout"] if isinstance(self.reviews, dict) else self.reviews
+            if "--paginate" not in argv:
+                raw = raw[: raw.find("\n") + 1] if "\n" in raw else raw
             modelled = _apply_reviews_jq(argv, raw)
```

</details>

Add a named assertion in `test/policy/crq/prReviewFindings.test.ts` that the reviews request argv includes `--paginate`. Doctrine I11 requires this GitHub pagination fact to be carried as a named test.
findings.title: Make the reviews fake drop later pages when `--paginate` is absent.

findings.body:
**Skip worktree creation for jobs that will not dispatch.**

`mark_stale` writes a terminal `STALE` result, but `process_item` still creates a detached worktree for that job before `process()` returns the stored result. The worktree is then never removed. Create it only for jobs that are still pending.

`drain_item` passes superseded jobs to `process_item`. `process_item` runs `git worktree add --detach` for every job that is not skipped, before it calls `process()`. `process()` returns the prior result without using the new tree when that result has no `retry_after`. `cleanup_harvested` returns `False` for any verdict other than `FIXED` or `NOT-FIXED`, so it never removes a `STALE` tree.

Use `pending()` to gate creation:

<details>
<summary>Proposed change</summary>

```diff
         wt = Path(config['worktree_root']) / ('crq-repair-' + item + '-' + job['job'])
-        if not wt.exists():
+        if pending(job['job']) and not wt.exists():
             p = command(['git', 'worktree', 'add', '--detach', str(wt), base], cwd=config['clone'])
```
</details>

`pending()` returns true when no `result.json` exists or when the stored result has `retry_after`. `process()` needs the tree only in those cases. Base chaining still works. It takes the base from `res['commits']` in the returned result, not from the tree.
findings.title: Skip worktree creation for jobs that will not dispatch.
